gloss: starting station; first station on a line

definitions.gloss: starting station; terminal station where a train line originates
definitions.explanation: The first station on a train line or the station where a particular train service begins its run. Passengers boarding here are guaranteed a seat.

examples.japanese: ここは{始発駅|しはつえき}だから{座|すわ}れる。
examples.english: Since this is the starting station, we can get seats.

examples.japanese: {始発駅|しはつえき}から{乗|の}れば{通勤|つうきん}ラッシュでも{座席|ざせき}が{確保|かくほ}できる。
examples.english: If you board from the starting station, you can secure a seat even during rush hour.

examples.japanese: この{路線|ろせん}の{始発駅|しはつえき}は{東京駅|とうきょうえき}で、{終点|しゅうてん}は{熱海駅|あたみえき}です。
examples.english: The starting station of this line is Tokyo Station, and the last stop is Atami Station.

notes:
Composed of {始発|しはつ} (first departure; originating) and {駅|えき} (station). The term refers specifically to the station where a train begins its run, not to a random stop along the way.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {始発駅|しはつえき}から{乗|の}る — to board from the starting station
- {始発駅|しはつえき}で{並|なら}ぶ — to line up at the starting station
- {路線|ろせん}の{始発駅|しはつえき} — the starting station of a line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {始発|しはつ} — first train/bus of the day (also used as a modifier meaning "originating")
- {終着駅|しゅうちゃくえき} / {終点|しゅうてん} — terminal station; last stop
- {起点|きてん} — starting point (more abstract; not limited to trains)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Tokyo and other major cities, living near a {始発駅|しはつえき} is valued by commuters because it guarantees a seat on the train. Some people choose apartments near starting stations specifically for this advantage.
